subject: Mathematics
central_question: How can we measure and compare the spread of ungrouped and grouped data around a central value?
in_scope_units: Introduction: why measures of central tendency alone do not fully describe data and why dispersion is needed.
Measures of dispersion and range as a first rough measure of variability.
Mean deviation about mean or median for ungrouped data.
Mean deviation for discrete and continuous frequency distributions, including cumulative frequency and median class methods.
Step-deviation shortcut for computing the mean used in mean-deviation calculations.
Limitations of mean deviation and the need for a measure based on squared deviations.
Variance and standard deviation for ungrouped data.
Variance and standard deviation for discrete and continuous frequency distributions.
Alternative and shortcut formulas for variance and standard deviation.
Effects of changing observations, correction of erroneous data, mixed examples and historical note.
banned_topics: Detailed calculation of quartile deviation, which the chapter explicitly excludes

known_pitfalls.claim: Two data sets with the same mean and median have the same variability.
known_pitfalls.correction: The batsmen example shows that equal mean and median can occur with very different spread, so a measure of dispersion is also required.

known_pitfalls.claim: Range measures how every observation is distributed around the mean.
known_pitfalls.correction: Range uses only the maximum and minimum values and gives only a rough idea of variability.

known_pitfalls.claim: Mean deviation is the ordinary mean of signed deviations from the mean.
known_pitfalls.correction: Signed deviations from the mean sum to zero; mean deviation uses absolute values of the deviations.

known_pitfalls.claim: For grouped data, divide by the number of distinct x-values or classes.
known_pitfalls.correction: Grouped-data formulas divide by N, the total frequency, not by the number of rows or classes.

known_pitfalls.claim: Variance and standard deviation have the same units.
known_pitfalls.correction: Variance is in squared units, while standard deviation is the positive square root of variance and has the same units as the observations.

known_pitfalls.claim: Adding a constant to every observation changes the variance.
known_pitfalls.correction: Adding or subtracting the same constant shifts the mean by that constant but leaves all deviations from the mean, and hence the variance, unchanged.

recommended_example_progression: Begin with the batsmen A and B data in Section 13.1 and the range calculation in Section 13.3.
Use NCERT Examples 1 and 3 for mean deviation about mean and median in ungrouped data.
Use NCERT Examples 4–7 for discrete and continuous grouped data, cumulative frequency and the median class.
Use NCERT Examples 8–10 to introduce variance and standard deviation for ungrouped, discrete and continuous data.
Use NCERT Examples 11–12 for alternative and step-deviation formulas.
Finish with NCERT Examples 13–16 for transformations, missing observations and correction of wrong data.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter contains Exercise 13.1 on mean deviation, Exercise 13.2 on variance and standard deviation, and the six-question Miscellaneous Exercise on Chapter 13.
